A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same unsupervised IRM work with PICA and VIAE. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian simulations and VIAE experiments on SMNIST and SCMNIST, including generation, environment transfer, and classifier accuracies over ten training runs.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original CelebA generation and environment-transfer results in Appendix D and Figures 7–8.

M1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a tentative PICA extension to more than two environments using intersected covariance-difference null spaces. Derivation and validation are explicitly deferred. The existing two-environment PICA, VIAE architecture, ELBO, and transfer heuristic remain unchanged; Appendix C analyzes those procedures.

E1.justification: Appendix D extends evaluation beyond the retained Gaussian simulation and modified MNIST datasets to real CelebA face images. Environments defined by the Male attribute support sensitive-attribute-conditioned generation and transfer, introducing a substantially different domain and application scenario.

E2.justification: The four linear probes in Table 1 are unchanged. Neither version evaluates external competing methods against VIAE, and the new CelebA experiments introduce no evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added CelebA transfer evaluation compares matched originals, within-environment reconstructions, and transferred outputs in Figure 8, adding a reconstruction control to the qualitative inspection. Existing synthetic sample counts, MNIST partitions, and linear-probe evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a qualitative disentanglement case study: Figures 7–8 vary the environmental latent component while examining preservation of facial structure, expression, and pose. Existing MNIST analyses remain, with no new systematic ablations or sensitivity sweeps.

E5.justification: Table 1 still reports mean accuracy and standard deviation over ten VIAE training runs. The new CelebA examples add no repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values and earlier graphical results are unchanged. Figures 7–8 add limited qualitative CelebA generation, reconstruction, and transfer results, described as partly preserving identity-related features. No comparable-setting numerical performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: New Appendix C derives linear-Gaussian conditional-mean encoders and a decoder, then motivates the existing averaging heuristic through an MSE objective. Appendix A.1 adds a tentative multi-environment formulation, and A.3 changes the trace-ratio estimate from equality to approximation. C.1 also introduces an incorrect lower-right block in its displayed matrix inverse.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central conclusion retain the same unsupervised IRM, PICA, VIAE, disentanglement, and transfer contributions. The conclusion adds a pointer to fairness applications without revising the central claims or asserting a new generalization guarantee.

C2.justification: Appendix D introduces a substantive fairness interpretation connecting environmental features to sensitive attributes and disentanglement to reduced discriminatory bias, while qualifying the demonstrations as preliminary. Appendix C adds a linear/MSE explanation of transfer and discusses dependence on noise and environment means. The existing unseen-environment limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D documents CelebA environment construction using the Male attribute and specifies generation with one fixed invariant latent and five draws from each environmental prior. Detailed CelebA training and preprocessing settings are not supplied, and the code availability statement is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Hardt, Price, and Srebro on equality of opportunity and Liu and colleagues on CelebA to support the fairness application. Existing references and the main related-work positioning are retained.

P1.justification: V2 revises wording and removes repeated model descriptions in Appendix A, clarifies notation in Appendix B, expands abbreviated section titles, and adds fairness cross-references. The abstract, introduction, and main narrative remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 7–8 add CelebA image grids and captions, with Figure 8 displayed on a separate page. Figures 1–6 and Table 1 remain intact; appendix additions produce localized equation and text reflow without a broader visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The realistic-data examples and explicit transfer analysis modestly strengthen v1's empirical scope and explanation of its heuristic. These gains are limited by qualitative-only fairness evidence, sparse training details, and the new block-inverse error in C.1, although the resulting conditional-mean encoder formula is correct. General unseen-environment guarantees remain unresolved.
